title: Ted Lewis, Ray Lopez and south side bands
summary: Steiner asks about Parenti, Ray Lopez and Dooley; Ashcraft knows them little and the tape ends mid-question about 35th Street bands.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well, Tony, uh... In the 30s was with Ted Lewis, and earlier was with, uh, in radio work at New York. But I don't think that he came north. Until about 30. In other words, he wasn't in the firsts. Um... There was a trumpet player by the name of Lopez.
Yes. But not, not very well. Uh, Lopez... Was it Ray?
It was of, uh, considerable influence to a slightly earlier generation than the Austin. Uh, Dooley talks about him. I guess Dooley played with him. Do you remember that Dooley had a brother in music?
No, I didn't know that. No?
Well, I've been trying to run him down. I hadn't been able to. They played out on the south side, around 35th Street, at the time that 35th Street was integrating.
I had the first colored band, then the second colored band, then he saw these...
